a-catalog-field-s-data-testid-derives-fr: A catalog field's data-testid derives from the AppForm shell's testIdPrefix plus the kebab-cased field name, and the message id is that plus -error. Passing an explicit testId prop overrides BOTH — which is how a migrated form keeps E2E ids byte-identical when the derived id would differ.
a-no-op-scaffold-in-api-src-does: A no-op scaffold in api/src does not compile: TreatWarningsAsErrors plus Roslynator RCS1163 and IDE0060 turn an unused parameter into a build error, so a placeholder handler or service method that ignores its arguments fails the build. A red-phase stub must consume every parameter - return a call that uses them and gets the answer wrong, rather than returning Task.CompletedTask.
a-spec-comparing-two-rendered-colours-mu: A spec comparing two rendered colours must not regex-parse getComputedStyle output — the fork palette is oklch and Chromium can serialize colours as oklch()/color(). Normalise by painting the colour string into a canvas 2d context (fillStyle, fillRect, getImageData) and reading the sRGB bytes.
a-wallow-module-s-feature-flag-is-read: A Wallow module's feature flag is read STRAIGHT OFF IConfiguration, not via IFeatureManager: WallowModules.IsModuleFlagEnabled reads the key "FeatureManagement:Modules.{module.Name}", treats an absent key as disabled, and THROWS InvalidOperationException at startup if the key is present but not a scalar bool (a filter-shaped flag would otherwise bind to null and silently disable the module). IsCore modules bypass the flag entirely (WallowModules.ResolveEnabledModules). AddFeatureManagement()/IFeatureManager are still registered deliberately -- they remain the documented extension point for a FORK's own flags, just not for Wallow's own module gating. That enabled set also gates the module's HTTP surface, not just its DI registrations: WallowModules.RemoveDisabledModuleApiParts, invoked from ConfigureApplicationPartManager, removes a disabled module's .Api assembly AssemblyPart from the ApplicationPartManager, so its controllers are excluded from routing/ApiExplorer/OpenAPI generation (404) instead of 500ing at request time from unresolved DI. Host code asks 'is module X on' with the compile-time-safe generic enabledModules.IsModuleEnabled<TModule>(), never a flag string literal.
a-zustand-store-or-queryclient-exported-: A zustand store or QueryClient exported from a workspace package must declare its runtime as a peerDependency, not a dependency: two resolved copies means two singletons and silent desync.
api-branding-json-is-the-fork-first-cano: packages/styles/branding.json is the fork-first canonical branding source (name, icon, tagline, repositoryUrl, docsUrl, theme tokens). It is frontend-only — no backend code has ever read it, and it does not live under api/. packages/styles owns the ForkBranding type, statically imports the JSON so Vite inlines it, and emits Tailwind v4 theme CSS from it; both React apps consume the same tokens, so changing the palette affects both simultaneously. scripts/generate-docs-theme.mjs reads it too (path passed as argv[1]).
api-tests-modules-identity-wallow-identi: api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Infrastructure/AdminBootstrapOptionsTests.cs is the repo's template for options-validation unit tests: plain options-record instantiation and assertion, no DI container or host bootstrap required. Use this pattern for any new *Options class validation tests instead of spinning up a WebApplicationFactory.
api-tests-wallow-tests-common-bases-dbco: api/tests/Wallow.Tests.Common/Bases/DbContextIntegrationTestBase.cs exposes CreateDbContextForTenant(tenantId, name) specifically to build a second DbContext scoped to a different tenant, for proving repository queries (including EF.CompileAsyncQuery compiled/static queries) don't leak across tenants. api/tests/Modules/Storage/Wallow.Storage.Tests/Integration/StoredFileRepositoryTests.cs is the reference example using this helper — mirror it for any new cross-tenant-leak test rather than building new scaffolding.
app-branding-is-a-separate-endpoint-from: App branding is a SEPARATE endpoint from app registration: POST /v1/identity/apps/{clientId}/branding (operationId ClientBrandingUpsertBranding), multipart/form-data with PascalCase DisplayName/Tagline/ThemeJson plus a lowercase logo file, keyed on a clientId that first exists in the register RESPONSE. The generated clientBrandingUpsertBranding already applies formDataBodySerializer and sends Content-Type null, so callers pass a plain body object — never hand-built FormData. The API 400s when DisplayName is blank, so a client must skip the call entirely rather than send an empty upsert.
apps-wallow-web-assert-a-mutation-s-cach: Assert a mutation's cache invalidation via expectSwept(spy, queryKey) from @bc-solutions-coder/testing/invalidation — it vi.waitFor's until a queryClient.invalidateQueries spy call's REAL predicate sweeps the given generated {op}QueryKey(...), so it fails if the sweep targets the wrong operation/tag. This is the repo's answer to 'generated query keys are flat, no prefix to assert by' — never compare the predicate object by identity or shape.
apps-wallow-web-dashboard-list-component: apps/wallow-web dashboard list components (AppList/InquiryList/OrganizationList) all follow one canonical shape: ui Card wrapping a ul[data-testid=X-table] of li[data-testid=X-item] rows, with MutedText-backed X-loading/X-empty-state states - OrganizationList (features/organizations/components/OrganizationList.tsx) is the documented CANONICAL template every later vertical copies.
attacker-supplied-query-key-lookups-use-: attacker-supplied-query-key-lookups-use-map-not-record: In wallow-auth screens, any map from an attacker-controlled query-string value to UI copy (canonical case: apps/wallow-auth/src/features/error/components/ErrorPage.tsx, /error?reason=<anything> is a URL anyone can construct and send a victim) MUST be a ReadonlyMap + .get(), never a plain object/Record + bracket lookup. A Record lookup resolves INHERITED keys, so ?reason=toString returns Object.prototype.toString — a FUNCTION handed to the renderer — and ?reason=constructor similar. Map.get only ever sees keys explicitly put in it. Typical port tests use a benign unrecognised reason (e.g. 'wat') which a Record survives, so this is NOT test-covered: do not 'simplify' the Map back to an object literal in review.
base-ui-popups-tooltip-and-by-constructi: Base UI popups (tooltip, and by construction the other dismissable popups) DO dismiss on outside press even when nothing blocks the pointer. A tooltip's portal contains only the positioner — no invisible blocker like a modal dialog's — which makes it easy to conclude wrongly that there is no outside-press dismissal either. There is: a press outside the popup fires onOpenChange(false, { reason: 'outside-press' }). Practical bite in a CONTROLLED popup driven from a button of the caller's own: that button's click opens the popup via the caller's handler and then dismisses it again in the same gesture, so an external control can close such a popup but cannot open one. A native element.click() does NOT reproduce this (it dispatches only a click, no pointerdown) — only a full pointer sequence does, so a probe using .click() will wrongly show an external toggle working.
bc-solutions-coder-forms-field-catalog-i: @bc-solutions-coder/forms field catalog is Text/Textarea/Select/Checkbox/Password only — there is no file/multi-select field. A control the catalog does not own still becomes a real form field via the form.AppField render-prop escape hatch (value + field.handleChange), not a plain uncontrolled child; RegisterAppForm's ScopeToggles is the in-repo template.
bd-parent-child-edge-direction: bd dep add A B --type parent-child makes B the PARENT of A (the edge reads 'A depends on B'). Wire an epic with 'bd dep add <child> <epic> --type parent-child'. Getting it backwards is silent: the tree still renders, but 'bd show <epic>' lists the tasks under PARENT instead of CHILDREN and 'bd epic status' reports 'No open epics found'. The beads:epic skill's own example documents this backwards.
browser-spec-sync-read-races-click-start: In Vitest browser mode, a SYNCHRONOUS assertion taken immediately after an awaited real-pointer interaction (userEvent.click/type) races any timer that interaction started, because the awaited Playwright round trip itself consumes wall-clock time — hundreds of ms under CPU contention. Fixture timer constants must therefore outlast a round trip, not merely be 'short for speed': packages/ui's toast specs failed at 80ms (toast auto-dismissed before the presence read) and at 40ms (promise re-typed to success before the loading read), and were raised to 500ms. Absence and settle assertions are a separate rule and must always poll (await expect.poll(...) in specs, waitFor(...) in Storybook play functions) because Base UI unmounts on an animation frame after an exit transition — read too early and the node is still in the document carrying data-ending-style. Asserting a NON-EVENT is the one case that needs a real wait instead of a poll, since a poll resolves on its first read.
csrf-delivery-pattern-synchronizer-token: CSRF delivery pattern: synchronizer token in session.csrfToken; non-HttpOnly double-submit cookie set on login; x-csrf-token header echoed by browser; user endpoint returns csrfToken. Validate on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE in proxy; GET/HEAD bypass.
docker-compose-test-project-collision: docker-compose.test.yml resolves to the SAME compose project name ('wallow', from docker/.env's COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME) as the base docker-compose.yml dev-infra stack, regardless of cwd (docker compose uses the compose file's own directory as project-directory by default). Running 'docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.test.yml down --remove-orphans' (what scripts/e2e.sh's teardown does) while the base dev-infra stack (postgres/valkey/garage/mailpit/alloy/docs/grafana-lgtm, container_names literal e.g. wallow-postgres) is up will REMOVE those base containers as orphans of the shared project — verified reproducing this. Named volumes are untouched (test uses its own test_-prefixed volume names), so data survives and 'cd docker && docker compose up -d' restores it, but the containers must be manually brought back up. Before/after running scripts/e2e.sh or any docker-compose.test.yml command, check 'docker ps' for the base stack and restart it if this wipes it.
docker-docker-compose-test-yml-and-docke: docker/docker-compose.test.yml and docker-compose.production.yml's wallow-auth/wallow-web services carry NO 'command:' override -- both rely entirely on their Dockerfile's CMD to launch the app, so changing how an app is started (e.g. TanStack Start's node .output/server/index.mjs vs tsx server.ts) only requires editing the Dockerfile, not the compose files, unless a compose-level env/port contract also changes.
dotnet-test-trx-behavior-verified-via-sc: dotnet test TRX behavior (verified via scratch repro, general .NET SDK fact not repo-specific code): on a COMPILE failure, 'dotnet test' exits nonzero and writes ZERO .trx files to --results-directory. On a successful build where a --filter matches 0 tests, 'dotnet test' exits 0 AND still writes a .trx file with Counters all zero (total=0 failed=0). Any script/tooling parsing TRX counters to decide pass/fail must also check the dotnet test process exit code (or trx-file count) to distinguish 'built fine, 0 tests matched' from 'failed to compile' — TOTAL==0 alone is not a reliable FAIL signal.
e2e-sh-stops-at-first-failing-suite: scripts/e2e.sh runs the three Playwright suites sequentially (wallow-auth, then wallow-web, then wallow-web cross-app) with no error tolerance, so a wallow-auth failure means the wallow-web and cross-app suites never run at all and the run reports no coverage for them. When the auth suite fails for a reason you have already triaged, re-run with E2E_KEEP_STACK=1 and drive the remaining two by hand against the kept stack: env E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5053 pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e (and test:e2e:cross-app).
expiresat-is-epoch-milliseconds-internal: expiresAt is epoch MILLISECONDS internally (NOT Unix seconds). The design doc says seconds but SDK deliberately keeps ms to avoid rewriting skew math. Document this in BffSession JSDoc. EXPIRY_SKEW_MS is used in proxy.ts refresh check.
hey-api-0-99-0-s-pluginconfigmap-does: hey-api 0.99.0's PluginConfigMap does not expose a framework-agnostic query-core plugin (only framework-specific ones like @tanstack/react-query are user-selectable), and its generated query keys are flat single-object arrays (e.g. [{ _id, baseUrl, path }]), not a hierarchical prefix factory -- invalidation must match on _id/tags via a curated module, not a keys-factory subtree sweep.
identity-membership-listing-covers-only-: Identity's membership listings cover two statuses only: OrganizationService.GetMembersAsync returns Active, MembershipReviewService.GetPendingAsync returns Pending. Nothing lists Suspended or Denied, so the reinstate and clear-denial endpoints have no list a UI could drive them from.
identity-role-writes-are-ambient-tenant-: UsersController.AssignRole and RemoveRole take no organization id: both write tenantContext.TenantId.Value, i.e. the CALLER's own organization. A screen keyed by an org route param must gate role controls on that param matching the caller's own org - OrganizationsController.GetAll already filters its result to exactly the caller's tenant, so its single row is the check. Without the gate a grant against a foreign org silently lands in the operator's own org and returns 204. InvitationsController.GetByTenant is the same shape: ambient tenant, no org-id parameter, so an invitations screen cannot be org-parameterised.
iron-webcrypto-1-2-1-s-seal-unseal: iron-webcrypto 1.2.1's seal()/unseal() support KEYED password rotation natively: seal()'s password param accepts 'password.Secret = { id?: string; secret: Password }' (embeds the id in the sealed blob), and unseal()'s password param accepts 'password.Hash = Record<string, Password|Secret|Specific>' (a key-id -> secret map) — unseal reads the id embedded by seal() and picks the matching map entry automatically; the caller never needs to try multiple keys manually. Verified in node_modules/.pnpm/iron-webcrypto@1.2.1/.../dist/index.d.ts. Used by packages/sdk/src/server/session.ts and txstate.ts for sealed BFF session/tx cookies.
iron-webcrypto-s-seal-unseal-used-by-pac: iron-webcrypto's seal()/unseal() (used by packages/sdk/src/server/session.ts and txstate.ts) default SealOptions.ttl to 0, meaning 'forever' — sealed cookie blobs never cryptographically expire unless callers explicitly pass a nonzero ttl (milliseconds) in the options spread. Any code calling iron-webcrypto's seal with just the bare `defaults` constant has this latent no-expiry bug; grep for `defaults` usage in packages/sdk/src/server/ to find all call sites.
iswallowerror-packages-sdk-is-designed-a: isWallowError (packages/sdk) is designed as a brand-check function, not instanceof -- module-graph duplication across bundlers/test runners breaks instanceof for error classes, so WallowError recognition must use a marker property instead.
layering-rule-packages-styles-tokens-pac: Layering rule: packages/styles (tokens) -> packages/ui (knows nothing about forms) -> packages/forms (imports ui, binds TanStack Form state) -> apps. forms must never be imported by ui; ui gains zero forms knowledge. If forms needs a look ui can't produce, fix lands in ui/styles first as a normal forms-unaware change.
mfa-endpoints-mfacontroller-return-busin: MFA endpoints (MfaController) return business failures as a RAW anon object { succeeded:false, error:'<code>' } via BadRequest/Unauthorized — NOT RFC7807 ProblemDetails. So React Query onError receives a body with NO .detail. Any error surface for MFA must fall back to mapping the .error code to a friendly message (no_auth_session/invalid_password/invalid_code/mfa_not_enabled/user_not_found) — reading only .detail always yields the generic fallback and hides the real reason. Applies to enrollTotp/confirmEnroll/disable/regenerateBackupCodes.
new-workspace-packages-need-two-dockerfi: New workspace packages need TWO Dockerfile COPY lines per consuming app (manifest before pnpm install, sources before the build RUN). Nothing local guards this any more — a missing line surfaces only when CI (or scripts/e2e.sh) builds the app images, so check the consuming apps' Dockerfiles whenever adding a package.
openapi-document-operation-transformer-p: OpenAPI document/operation transformer pipeline lives in api/src/Wallow.Api/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs (registered in AddApiServices via options.AddDocumentTransformer/AddOperationTransformer), with internal static transformer methods at the bottom of the same file and exemplar unit tests in api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensionsTests.cs (construct a fake OpenApiOperationTransformerContext/OpenApiDocumentTransformerContext with a ControllerActionDescriptor + call the internal static method directly — no TestServer needed). Microsoft.OpenApi 2.10.0 API notes verified via package XML docs: OpenApiOperation.Tags is a HashSet<OpenApiTagReference> (compare via .Name); OpenApiOperation.OperationId is a plain settable string; OpenApiDocument.Paths holds IOpenApiPathItem whose .Operations is a dict of OpenApiOperation; OpenApiDocumentTransformerContext exposes DescriptionGroups (ApiDescriptionGroup list); OpenApiOperationTransformerContext also exposes .Document.
openiddict-app-lookup-pattern-in-this-re: OpenIddict app lookup pattern in this repo: applicationManager.FindByClientIdAsync(clientId, ct) returning object? application is the established per-client lookup (see ClientTenantResolver.cs, ScopeSubsetValidator.cs, OpenIddictDeveloperAppService.cs, AuthorizationController.cs) — prefer it over applicationManager.ListAsync(null,null,ct) (iterates ALL registered OIDC apps) whenever a specific client_id is known, to avoid cross-client data bleed.
organizationscontrollercrosstenanttests-: OrganizationsControllerCrossTenantTests.cs (api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Api/Controllers/) maintains a reflection-checked inventory: a _endpointPermissions dictionary (method name -> required PermissionType) plus a name-dispatch switch statement, one entry per org-scoped controller method. Its EveryOrganizationScopedEndpoint_AppearsInTheInventory test fails if a new OrganizationsController endpoint isn't added to both. Any new endpoint on that controller must update this file or the cross-tenant gate test silently ignores it.
package-versions-for-react-react-dom-tan: Package versions for react, react-dom, @tanstack/react-form, @tanstack/react-query and zustand come from the 'react' pnpm catalog; @tanstack/react-start, react-router and react-router-ssr-query from the 'start' catalog. Declare catalog:<name>, never a literal. The one exception: a LIBRARY peering on @tanstack/react-router uses a literal caret range against the apps' exact pin, which is correct practice rather than drift.
packages-config-is-the-vite-preset-packa: packages/config is the VITE PRESET package (./vite/library, ./vite/app) — never built, never published, exports point at src/ permanently. It is NOT an env-validation package; that is packages/env. packages/config must not gain app-shaped dependencies (Start, nitro, plugin-react, @bc-solutions-coder/styles), the last of which would cycle since styles builds with it.
packages-styles-src-theme-css-test-ts-pa: packages/styles/src/theme-css.test.ts parses styles.css's @theme block by splitting the body on ';' and anchoring each fragment with /^\s*--[\w-]+/. A comment line placed inside @theme immediately above a declaration lands in that declaration's fragment, breaks the anchor, and makes the token vanish from the parse, failing the token pins. Put explanatory comments in the file header above @theme, or after the last declaration's ';'. A comment inside @theme must never contain '}' — the block regex is [^}]*.
packages-testing-src-render-with-wallow-: packages/testing/src/render-with-wallow.tsx exports renderWithWallow, which wraps a component in a memory router plus a QueryClientProvider plus the SDK test harness in one call. Any app component test needing router context (TanStack Link, useRouterState, etc.) should use this existing helper instead of hand-building a new router-context test wrapper.
packages-ui-base-ui-field-context-packag: packages/ui Base UI Field context (packages/ui/src/components/field/field.tsx) propagates id/aria-invalid/aria-describedby/data-invalid/data-disabled to ANY Field-context-aware descendant placed directly inside <Field>/<Field.Root> -- not just <Field.Control>. Verified for Input (Base UI's Input IS Field.Control under the hood), and Base UI's CheckboxRoot/SelectTrigger both call useFieldRootContext/useFormContext directly too. So a catalog field wrapper can nest a bare <Input>/<Checkbox.Root>/<Select.Trigger> inside <Field><Field.Label/>...</Field> and get full association with zero extra plumbing; Field.Error only renders when its 'match' prop is satisfied (bare 'match' = always-show; an 'invalid' root alone does not produce a message).
packages-ui-ships-both-a-root-barrel-bc: packages/ui ships BOTH a root barrel (@bc-solutions-coder/ui) and per-component subpath exports (@bc-solutions-coder/ui/<name>) from the same Vite preserveModules build (dist/ mirrors src/ 1:1, sideEffects:false) — the folder structure under src/components/ IS the subpath export structure.
preregisteredclientoptions-clients-api-s: PreRegisteredClientOptions.Clients (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Options/PreRegisteredClientOptions.cs) is bound directly from api/seed.json's "clients" JSON array via Wallow.SeederService/Program.cs's SeedOptions.Clients mapping — there is no separate "PreRegisteredClients" appsettings section in any tracked appsettings*.json. This means seed.json's client array order IS the same positional index the Clients__<N>__... env-var overrides in docker-compose*.yml target; inserting/deleting a seed.json client entry shifts every later index and requires updating all docker-compose Clients__N overrides in lockstep.
react-query-drops-mutate-vars-onsuccess-: react-query drops mutate(vars, { onSuccess }) callbacks when the observing component unmounts, so a follow-up mutation fired from a form whose success view REPLACES the form must be owned by the surviving parent component, not by the form body.
renaming-a-theme-colour-key-in-api-brand: Renaming a theme colour key in api/branding.json silently disables any per-OAuth-client themeJson override that still uses the old key. packages/styles/src/branding.ts mergeClientBranding merges client vars over fork vars BY KEY NAME, and CSS var() fallback is first-defined-wins, so a fork emitting the new name and a stored client row emitting the old name produce two separate custom properties and the fork's value wins. No @theme fallback chain can express the correct precedence. Treat any branding theme-key rename as breaking for stored client branding, not just for merge=ours fork files.
run-tests-sh-s-default-and-per-module: run-tests.sh's default (and per-module) filters include Testcontainers-backed suites (Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure.Tests/Auditing/AuditInterceptorTests via AuditInterceptorFixture, and any WallowApiFactory-based integration test e.g. Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests) that spin up real postgres:18-alpine (and redis) Docker containers. If Docker Desktop isn't running, these fail with DotNet.Testcontainers.Builders.DockerUnavailableException at fixture-constructor time -- a pure environment gap, not a code regression. Start Docker Desktop ('open -a Docker') and wait for 'docker info' to succeed before treating such failures as real.
scripts-check-exports-sh-names-its-packa: scripts/check-exports.sh names its packages in an explicit bash array. A new package is NOT covered until it is added there, so 'pnpm check:exports is clean' passes vacuously for any package missing from the array.
sdk-api-scope-delimiter-contract-appscon: SDK/API scope-delimiter contract: AppsController.GetConsentInfo (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/AppsController.cs) parses the ?scopes= query param by splitting on a single SPACE (OAuth's own scope-delimiter convention), pinned by AppsControllerTests.cs. Any client building that query string (e.g. AuthClient.getConsentInfo in packages/sdk/src/auth-client.ts) must space-join scopes, not comma-join, or scopes silently fail to resolve against scopeManager.FindByNameAsync and render as one garbled entry.
sdk-wallowerror-constructor-call-sites-g: SDK WallowError constructor call sites (grep -rn "new WallowError" packages/sdk/src): two sites parse a real upstream problem-details body -- packages/sdk/src/server/errors.ts parseProblemDetails() (server-side, used by proxy.ts's upstreamError) and packages/sdk/src/runtime-config.ts toWallowError() (browser interceptor, wired via wireWallowErrorInterceptor in create-sdk.ts). Both have their OWN independent readCode()/readTraceId()-style helpers (not shared) that probe extensions.code / extensions.traceId with flattened fallbacks -- any new WallowError field sourced from problem details (e.g. RFC 7807 'errors' member) must be wired at BOTH sites separately. Other 'new WallowError' sites in packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.ts (network fault, CSRF-redirect auth failure, CSRF token mismatch) are synthetic (no parsed body) and never need that wiring.
tailwind-colour-tokens-in-packages-style: Tailwind colour tokens in packages/styles/styles.css map onto bare custom properties with no values; the values come only from renderThemeStyle(forkResolvedBranding). A vitest browser project that loads the Tailwind entry but not that theme computes every colour utility as transparent/inherited, so colour and contrast assertions there are vacuous.
tailwind-v4-resolves-source-relative-to-: Tailwind v4 resolves @source relative to the declaring stylesheet, so a test-time Tailwind entry cannot be hoisted into a shared package: every consumer keeps its own root-level vitest-styles.css. Only the theme <style> injection is shareable.
tailwind-v4-source-scanning-for-workspac: Tailwind v4 @source scanning for workspace UI packages: each package that ships scannable component source ships its OWN <pkg>/source.css at package ROOT (mirroring packages/styles/styles.css's root-level placement + files:['dist','styles.css'|'source.css'] + a raw passthrough export entry with no types/import keys) declaring @source "./src"; relative to itself, and every consuming app's CSS entry adds one @import line for it. Tailwind v4 skips node_modules and @source resolves relative to the declaring stylesheet, so this explicit per-package declaration is required -- there is no existing packages/styles helper/export that already does this for you.
tanstack-form-tanstack-form-core-1-33-2: TanStack Form (@tanstack/form-core 1.33.2) form.setErrorMap({ onServer: X }) accepts X shaped as GlobalFormValidationError = { form?: unknown; fields: Partial<Record<fieldName, unknown>> } (top-level 'form'+'fields' keys, verified by reading FormApi.js setErrorMap/isGlobalFormValidationError/normalizeError source, not docs). Field-level values in 'fields' may be a plain string OR a string array -- field.state.meta.errors is built via Object.values(fieldMeta.errorMap).filter(defined).flat(1), so an array value spreads into separate top-level error entries. No StandardSchemaV1Issue wrapping is required for server-pushed errors; plain strings/string-arrays work directly. Only fields already mounted (registered via form.Field/AppField) at call time receive the update.
tanstack-route-component-cannot-be-rende: tanstack-route-component-cannot-be-render-ed-bare-if-it-reads-search: In @tanstack/react-router (verified v1.170.18 source + empirically), routerContext defaults to null, useRouter returns that null (only console.warns), and useMatch:156 dereferences router.stores unconditionally. So ANY router hook (Route.useSearch/useParams/useNavigate...) throws 'Cannot read properties of null (reading stores)' when the component is rendered outside a RouterProvider. strict:false / shouldThrow:false do NOT help — they gate the missing-MATCH path, which is never reached. CONSEQUENCE for wallow-auth/wallow-web screen-port tests: the 'renders the real screen in place of the route-placeholder' test may only use the bare render(<RouteComponent/>) pattern for routes that read NO search (ForgotPasswordForm.test.tsx). Any route with validateSearch (login, consent, logout, mfa/*, invitation, verify-email/*, error, reset-password...) MUST use the memory-router harness: createRootRoute() + rootRoute.addChildren([route.update({id,path,getParentRoute})]) + createRouter({routeTree, history:createMemoryHistory({initialEntries:['/path?x=1']})}) + render(<RouterProvider router={router}/>). Canonical example already in repo: apps/wallow-auth/src/features/reset-password/components/ResetPasswordForm.test.tsx renderRouteAt(). It also pins MORE (proves the query string threads through validateSearch into the screen's props). Do NOT 'fix' this by giving the route component a no-router fallback branch — that is dead code in production existing only for a test.
tanstack-route-directory-creates-no-layo: In this repo's TanStack file routing, a route DIRECTORY with no route.tsx creates path nesting and no layout component - routes/dashboard/organizations/ has neither organizations.tsx nor route.tsx and its children attach straight to the /dashboard layout. But a sibling FILE named after the directory (organizations/$orgId.tsx beside an $orgId/ directory) IS promoted to the layout for those children, so a leaf route with no <Outlet/> must be moved to <param>/index.tsx before siblings are added. The trailing-underscore un-nesting convention works in the installed generator but has no precedent here.
tanstack-router-default-search-parser-js: TanStack Router's default search parser JSON-parses every query value BEFORE validateSearch sees it, so ?flag=true arrives as the BOOLEAN true (and numbers arrive as numbers), not the string 'true'. validateSearch implementations must accept the JSON-parsed types, not raw strings. (Reconstructed from a truncated preview after accidental deletion; core trap verified against TanStack docs behavior.)
tanstack-router-redirect-to-an-unregiste: In @tanstack/react-router (verified on 1.170.x), redirect() accepts BOTH 'to' (resolved against the typed/registered route tree) and 'href'. Redirecting to a path NOT registered in the route tree via 'to' fails/mis-resolves — use 'href' for unregistered/external destinations. (Reconstructed from a truncated preview after accidental deletion.)
tanstack-router-update-only-accepts-upda: TanStack Router .update() only accepts UpdatableRouteOptions fields (validateSearch/shouldReload/context/ssr/beforeLoad/loaderDeps/remountDeps/loader) -- id/path/getParentRoute live on BaseRouteOptions and are NOT valid .update() args per @tanstack/router-core's route.d.ts. The official file-route codegen itself bypasses this with '.update({id, path, getParentRoute} as any)' (see any app's routeTree.gen.ts). Any hand-written test harness that reparents a createFileRoute() route onto a throwaway rootRoute for rendering (the 'renderRouteAt(url)' pattern used across apps/wallow-auth/src/features/*/components/*.test.tsx) must match that same 'as any' escape hatch rather than inventing a different workaround -- it mirrors the sanctioned codegen pattern, not a new suppression.
tanstack-start-nitro-build-needs-use-syn: TanStack Start + nitro production builds must alias use-sync-external-store/shim to react in vite.config.ts resolve.alias. The shim is CJS reached via @base-ui/utils -> @base-ui/react; rolldown leaves its require("react") as a runtime __require, so the built server loads a SECOND React beside the bundled one. Every Base UI component reading a store (useIsHydrating: Tabs/Checkbox/Select) then throws 'Invalid hook call' + 'Cannot read properties of null (reading useSyncExternalStore)' during SSR and the page degrades to an empty client-only document. Dev mode is unaffected, so this only shows up against node .output/server/index.mjs. Use ANCHORED REGEX finds (/^use-sync-external-store\/shim$/u and the /index.js variant), never a bare string alias: string aliases match by prefix and would rewrite .../shim/with-selector to the nonexistent react/with-selector. React 19 ships useSyncExternalStore natively so the shim is dead weight. resolve.dedupe and optimizeDeps.include do NOT fix it. Applies to every Wallow Start app using @bc-solutions-coder/ui.
tanstack-start-react-start-1-168-x-start: TanStack Start (react-start 1.168.x / start-plugin-core 1.171.x) basepath behavior, verified by spiking a real based build: (1) server route handlers receive the ORIGINAL, still-prefixed Request — Start matches the route against the basepath-STRIPPED pathname (createStartHandler handleServerRoutes -> executeRewriteInput(router.rewrite,url); router-core rewrite.js rewriteBasepath.input) but never rewrites request.url, so any handler that reads request.url must strip the prefix itself. (2) tanstackStart's router.basepath is a sibling key of routeFileIgnorePattern inside the same router:{} object, and when unset it is DERIVED from Vite's base (planning.js deriveRouterBasepath returns configuredBasepath ?? publicBase trimmed of slashes). (3) Vite base alone is NOT enough with nitro/vite: base rewrites asset URLs in the HTML but nitro keeps SERVING the client output dir at the root, so every script/stylesheet 404s and the page never hydrates — nitro() needs its own baseURL option set to the same prefix.
tanstack-start-ssr-shell-no-headcontent-: tanstack-start-ssr-shell-no-headcontent-scripts: In TanStack Router/Start (@tanstack/react-router 1.170.x), HeadContent and Scripts both THROW under react-dom/server renderToString when rendered outside a live RouterProvider ('useRouter must be used inside a RouterProvider'; reads .options of null). A __root shell that must be renderToString-able in isolation (e.g. an SSR unit test that only mocks Outlet) must be hook-free: plain <html>/<head>/<body> + <Outlet/>. Add Scripts/HeadContent only once hydration wiring + a RouterProvider are in place.
the-auth-audit-trail-authauditrecord-aut: The auth audit trail (AuthAuditRecord -> AuthAuditEntry -> auth_audit.auth_audit_entries) is written by Wolverine handlers in Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Handlers/AuthAuditEventHandlers.cs, one static Handle overload per integration event, and EventType is a free-form PascalCase string rather than an enum. Adding a field to the trail means touching AuthAuditRecord, AuthAuditEntry, AuthAuditService.RecordAsync and the AuthAudit migration together - the record and the entity are separate types and nothing fails if the service forgets to copy between them.
the-net-10-microsoft-aspnetcore-openapi-: The .NET 10 Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi XML-comment source generator intercepts AddOpenApi and silently registers one extra OPERATION transformer (a generated XmlCommentOperationTransformer) plus a schema transformer, because api/Directory.Build.props sets GenerateDocumentationFile=true for every project. It adds NO document transformer. Any test asserting an exact operation-transformer count on OpenApiOptions must therefore expect hand-registered count + 1; document-transformer counts are unaffected. Verify with: strings on the built Wallow.Api.dll, look for OpenApiXmlCommentSupport_generated ... XmlCommentOperationTransformer.
the-one-list-of-wallow-s-seven-modules: The one list of Wallow's seven modules is WallowModuleRegistry.All in api/src/Wallow.Modules.Registry — a host-tier project (sibling to Wallow.Api/Wallow.MigrationService, deliberately NOT under api/src/Shared/, which would cycle because modules reference Shared). Both hosts read it: Wallow.Api filters it through IFeatureManager, Wallow.MigrationService takes it unfiltered so a disabled module's schema still migrates. Adding a module means adding one entry there plus a ProjectReference in that one csproj — never a second array in a host.
the-sidebar-token-family-color-sidebar-f: The sidebar-* token family (--color-sidebar / -foreground / -accent, mapped in packages/styles/styles.css from api/branding.json's sidebar/sidebarForeground/sidebarAccent) is the theme's GENERAL INVERTED-SURFACE family, not a sidebar-only one. It deliberately paints the dashboard rail and drawer, PublicLayout's footer band, LandingPage's steps band, and the outline-CTA hover. The name is retained deliberately; renaming it to inverse-* was considered and rejected.
tsx-jsx-classic-runtime-gotcha-the-stand: tsx-jsx-classic-runtime-gotcha: the standalone 'tsx' runner (esbuild) does NOT pick up jsx:'react-jsx' from apps/wallow-web/tsconfig.json — it fails to read the JSONC comments / extends chain and defaults to the CLASSIC runtime, so hook-free React components with no 'import React' crash at runtime with 'React is not defined'. Fixes: run JSX through Vite/@vitejs/plugin-react (what dev-server.ts does) OR pass a comment-free tsconfig via TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH. vitest/tsc read the commented tsconfig fine; only tsx is affected.
vitest-resetmodules-breaks-instanceof-ac: vitest-resetmodules-breaks-instanceof-across-graphs: In packages/sdk tests, a helper doing vi.resetModules() + dynamic import(./mod) re-evaluates the WHOLE graph of ./mod, including transitively-imported class modules like src/server/errors.ts. Any class (e.g. WallowError) is then minted a SECOND time, so it is NOT identical to the one the test file imported statically at top level — expect(x).toBeInstanceOf(WallowError) fails with the confusing 'expected WallowError: ... to be an instance of WallowError'. Fix: drop vi.resetModules() when the module under test has no module-level state (a pure factory like createAuthClient() does not), since vi.clearAllMocks() in beforeEach already resets vi.mock() spy registries; or re-import the class from the fresh graph and assert against that. Do NOT patch the production class with Symbol.hasInstance to paper over it. Diagnostic tell: the thrown value prints with the right name and fields but instanceof still fails.
wallow-apps-wallow-web-feature-dirs-each: Wallow apps/wallow-web feature dirs each own a thin api.ts re-export seam (see apps/wallow-web/src/features/organizations/api.ts) that is THE ONLY data import a feature's components use - it re-exports exactly the generated {op}Options/{op}Mutation/{op}QueryKey artifacts the feature needs from @bc-solutions-coder/sdk/query (or raw @bc-solutions-coder/sdk for the rare no-generated-artifact case), with a doc comment explaining the seam. A co-located api.test.ts asserts identity (expect(api.x).toBe(query.x) via a namespace import); the lint override at apps/**/src/features/*/api.test.ts already whitelists importing the raw/query entry there.
wallow-architecture-tests-already-projec: Wallow.Architecture.Tests already ProjectReferences both Wallow.Api and Wallow.MigrationService (and every module's four layers), so a single behavioural test in that project can compare runtime state from both hosts without new project references. It reaches WallowModules.cs via reflection today (Assembly.Load + GetMethod on the public static AddWallowModules), not InternalsVisibleTo — there is no InternalsVisibleTo anywhere in Wallow.Api's csproj yet.
wallow-auth-mfaenroll-qr-the-api-returns: wallow-auth MfaEnroll QR: the API returns qrUri as an otpauth:// URI STRING (see MfaService.cs), NOT a renderable data-URI/image — any QR must be drawn client-side. apps/wallow-auth uses qrcode.react rendering <svg> (NOT <canvas>). The assertable seam is data-qr-uri={the API's qrUri} on the mfa-enroll-qr element — assert that, never QR pixels, so the library stays swappable. Reuse qrcode.react if any other screen needs a QR; do not add a second QR lib.
wallow-auth-oidc-passthrough-prefixes: apps/wallow-auth's OIDC surface is createApiPassthrough() from @bc-solutions-coder/sdk/server/passthrough, wired via apps/wallow-auth/src/shared/lib/api-passthrough.server.ts. It mounts /v1/**, /connect/** AND /.well-known/** — OIDC clients repointing OIDC_ISSUER at the wallow-auth origin rely on default discovery at ${OIDC_ISSUER}/.well-known/openid-configuration working through this passthrough. Any change to the prefix allowlist must keep /.well-known/** or OIDC discovery 404s (this regression has happened before).
wallow-auth-s-consent-screen-apps-wallow: wallow-auth's consent screen (apps/wallow-auth/src/features/consent/components/ConsentScreen.tsx) was ported verbatim from the OLD BLAZOR Consent.razor 'oracle', including that oracle's bugs where they existed (e.g. requesting consent-info with Array.Empty<string>() instead of the real requested scopes) - do not assume behavior matching the oracle is therefore correct; the oracle itself could be buggy and the port comments say so explicitly when it is.
wallow-auth-same-origin-baseurl-apps-wal: wallow-auth same-origin baseUrl: apps/wallow-auth's server surface (src/shared/lib/api-passthrough.server.ts, a pure reverse-proxy preset from @bc-solutions-coder/sdk/server/passthrough) mounts on /v1/**, /connect/**, and /.well-known/** at root via TanStack Start server routes. So wallow-auth must configure the BFF client with baseUrl:'/'; the SDK's '/api' default (correct for wallow-web's BFF) would 404 every call. credentials:'include' is what carries the auth cookie.
wallow-cookie-secure-flag-convention-man: Wallow cookie Secure-flag convention: manually-built Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.CookieOptions (Response.Cookies.Append) should set Secure = httpContext.Request.IsHttps, never a hardcoded true/false. This mirrors CookieSecurePolicy.SameAsRequest (used by ConfigureApplicationCookie in api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Extensions/IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs) and is safe in production because Wallow.Api/Program.cs registers UseForwardedHeaders(XForwardedFor|XForwardedProto) before auth middleware, so Request.IsHttps reflects the real scheme even behind a TLS-terminating proxy. Known other offender with the same hardcoded-Secure=true bug (not yet filed/fixed): api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/AccountController.cs ExternalLoginState cookie.
wallow-ef-enum-column-convention-for-enu: Wallow EF enum-column convention: for enum-typed properties (e.g. OrgMemberRole, InvitationStatus), use .HasConversion<string>().HasMaxLength(N).IsRequired() in the IEntityTypeConfiguration — see InvitationConfiguration.cs and ScimSyncLogConfiguration.cs in api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/. Do not store enums as int.
wallow-generated-react-query-artifacts-l: Wallow generated react-query artifacts live in packages/sdk/src/generated/@tanstack/react-query.gen.ts, named {operation}Options() for reads, {operation}Mutation() for writes, {operation}QueryKey() for the key alone. Never guess a name - grep that file. Generated mutation variables are the full request object ({ body, path, query }), not a bare body - this is a different call-site shape than a hand-rolled mutationFn.
wallow-golden-path-docs-integrations-bff: Wallow golden path: docs/integrations/bff-pattern.md prescribes requesting scopes 'openid profile email offline_access'; the TS SDK (packages/sdk/.../config.ts:105) requires a CONFIDENTIAL client (secret), never a public client. Any client-provisioning endpoint meant to support the BFF pattern (AppsController) must allow that exact scope set and return a confidential client with one-time secret display.
wallow-keyed-isettingsservice-pattern-ap: Wallow keyed ISettingsService pattern: api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure/Settings/SettingsServiceExtensions.cs's AddSettings<TDbContext,TRegistry>(moduleKey) is the only path that registers AddKeyedSingleton<ISettingRegistry> and AddKeyedScoped<ISettingsService> for a module; it's constrained to 'TDbContext : TenantAwareDbContext<TDbContext>'. Any module DbContext that can't inherit that base (e.g. one that must inherit ASP.NET Core Identity's IdentityDbContext<TUser,TRole,TKey>) cannot call AddSettings<> at all -- it won't compile, not just fail at runtime. Storage is currently the only real caller of AddSettings<>.
wallow-loggermessage-log-content-asserti: Wallow [LoggerMessage] log-content assertions: the backend's [LoggerMessage] methods compile through the Microsoft.Gen.Logging generator (from Microsoft.Extensions.Telemetry.Abstractions), not the classic Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Generators path. The generated body grabs LoggerMessageHelper.ThreadLocalState, calls logger.Log(...), then immediately calls state.Clear(). So asserting log CONTENT from an NSubstitute ILogger's recorded call arguments never works: args[2].ToString() comes back empty and invoking the recorded formatter renders every parameter as '(null)', because the thread-local state was already cleared. To assert on log messages, use a real capturing ILogger implementation that calls formatter(state, exception) INSIDE its Log method. This also makes Wallow.Tests.Common LoggerAssertionExtensions.ShouldHaveLoggedMessage (which reads state.ToString() off recorded calls) unreliable for source-generated log methods. Asserting only LogLevel/EventId from recorded calls is still fine.
wallow-monorepo-apps-wallow-auth-and-app: Wallow monorepo: apps/wallow-auth and apps/wallow-web are TanStack Start apps, each with exactly ONE vite.config.ts (tanstackStart + react + nitro + wallowStyles) that serves both dev and production builds. There is no separate vite.ssr.config.ts and no hand-rolled dev-server.ts anymore — TanStack Start's Vite plugin owns the dev server, SSR, and route codegen, and 'vite build' emits a Nitro server bundle (.output/server/index.mjs). Any Tailwind/publicDir change is made in the single vite.config.ts only.
wallow-multi-tenancy-landmine-tenantsave: Wallow multi-tenancy landmine: TenantSaveChangesInterceptor (api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Kernel/MultiTenancy/TenantSaveChangesInterceptor.cs) overwrites the TenantId property of ANY Added/Modified ITenantScoped entity on SaveChanges, forcing it to the ambient tenant (DbContext.CurrentTenantId / ITenantContext / AmbientTenant.Current) regardless of what the entity constructor set. Any code path that needs to persist an entity whose TenantId differs from the caller's ambient tenant (e.g. minting a brand-new tenant/Organization) must call dbContext.SetTenant(newTenantId) before SaveChangesAsync, or the interceptor will silently stomp it.
wallow-net-api-emits-rfc-7807-problemdet: Wallow .NET API emits RFC 7807 ProblemDetails (status/title/detail/type/instance) but puts the machine-readable error code in extensions.code, NOT a top-level code field (see GlobalExceptionHandler.cs, ResultExtensions.cs). Any client-side ProblemDetails parser must read code from extensions.code with a synthetic UNKNOWN fallback.
wallow-seederservice-registers-a-nullmes: Wallow.SeederService registers a NullMessageBus as IMessageBus (api/src/Wallow.SeederService/NullMessageBus.cs) because the seeder never dispatches Wolverine messages — its InvokeAsync<T> throws NotSupportedException. Any seeder logic that needs Identity Application-layer command handlers (e.g. BootstrapAdminHandler) cannot invoke them via IMessageBus; the seeder must call the underlying Infrastructure services (e.g. IBootstrapAdminService) directly, replicating handler decision logic inline if needed.
wallow-tenant-model-organization-is-the-: Wallow tenant model: Organization IS the tenant — there is no separate Tenant entity. Organization.Create is the SINGLE place a tenant id is minted (org.Id == TenantId by construction); PreRegisteredClientSyncService must route seed-derived org creation through that same path rather than minting ids ad hoc.
wallow-test-project-pattern-for-exposing: Wallow test project pattern for exposing private/internal members to tests: add <InternalsVisibleTo Include="<TestProjectName>" /> to the source project's .csproj ItemGroup (see api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure.csproj) and mark the target member internal (not private).
wallow-web-e2e-routes-spec-excludes-dash: apps/wallow-web/e2e/routes.spec.ts is a BACKEND-FREE reachability gate and deliberately excludes /dashboard/** because those routes are auth-gated - its routes array is ["/", "/bff-demo"] and its header says so. Adding a new dashboard route to it makes the gate redirect to OIDC and fail. New dashboard routes need routeTree.gen.ts regenerated and committed (route-tree-drift.yml), NOT an entry there.
wallow-web-query-error-state-pattern-the: wallow-web-query-error-state-pattern: the canonical 'query gets an error state' pattern in apps/wallow-web (InquiryDetail.tsx, features/inquiries/components/InquiryDetail.tsx:66-96) is: derive `const value = query.data ?? null`, and ONLY when `value === null` branch further on `query.isError` to render an ErrorBanner with `errorText(query.error, fallback)` (apps/wallow-web/src/shared/lib/error-text.ts) -- this avoids blanking a screen that has cached data on a background refetch failure, and avoids conflating 'not found' (data resolved null) with 'errored' (query actually failed).
wallow-web-s-e2e-reachability-gate-apps-: wallow-web's E2E reachability gate (apps/wallow-web/e2e/routes.spec.ts) lists routes in a plain string[] array with a header comment documenting WHY each route is included/excluded; wallow-auth's parallel file (apps/wallow-auth/e2e/routes.spec.ts) is the fuller reference pattern including a 404-not-found test. Both assert data-app-ready='true' hydration and no backend dependency for reachability-only specs.
wallow-web-ssr-safe-redirect-pattern-for: wallow-web SSR-safe redirect pattern for unauthenticated gated routes: when a beforeLoad guard needs to send an unauthenticated visitor to the BFF login (an external endpoint like /bff/login, NOT a route registered in the TanStack route tree), throw redirect({ href: `/bff/login?returnTo=...` }) from @tanstack/react-router -- works identically during SSR (thrown as a Response) and CSR (router navigation). Do NOT call the SDK's browser-only login()/logout() (packages/sdk/src/auth.ts, bare 'location.href = ...') from a beforeLoad/loader that can run server-side -- Node has no global 'location' and it throws, turning the route into a 500. login()/logout() are safe only from client-only call sites (event handlers, effects).
wallow-workspace-packages-packages-sdk-p: Wallow workspace packages (packages/sdk, packages/styles, packages/testing, packages/ui) all share one build shape: Vite 8 (Rolldown) library-mode bundles JS only (rollupOptions.external excludes all non-relative imports so peer/runtime deps never get bundled), then a separate 'tsc -p tsconfig.build.json' (native tsc --emitDeclarationOnly CLI, not the bundler's programmatic API) emits .d.ts — because TS7's stable programmatic API doesn't exist yet. package.json scripts are always: build = 'vite build && tsc -p tsconfig.build.json', test = 'vitest run', test:watch = 'vitest', typecheck = 'tsc --noEmit'. Every package.json exports map entry needs a matching vite.config.ts lib.entry key (named entries for fixed subpaths like sdk's './server', or preserveModules for wildcard subpaths). packages/sdk is the reference template for this shape — its CLAUDE.md says so explicitly.
when-migrating-a-form-to-bc-solutions-co: When migrating a form to @bc-solutions-coder/forms's useAppForm, generated *Mutation({client}) factories (packages/sdk/src/generated/@tanstack/react-query.gen.ts) return ONLY {mutationFn}, no baked-in onSuccess - tag-sweep invalidation and any post-success side effect (form.reset(), lifting response data to local state for a gated success view) belong together in useAppForm's own onSuccess option, since useAppForm does not expose the raw mutation instance (isSuccess/data) to the caller.
